articles.title: Prizm Arctic
articles.summary: Fine pale blue-grey speckle, like frosted ice crystals or static snow, satin sheen with heavy sparkle throughout. Reads as light icy blue-grey with a crackled dark seam network and white frost flashes; a cold, glittery, busy pale blue.
articles.what: Up close: Pale ice-blue pebbles packed tightly, each 10-25 px, striped inside with fine ribbed lines like scales or shells. Dark slate cracks run between them, and thin white fracture lines branch across the cells in patches. From a distance: Reads as light icy blue-grey with a crackled dark seam network and white frost flashes; a cold, glittery, busy pale blue. Measured spec (average): metal 219, roughness 80, coat 233. Shine: satin. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Prizm Arctic" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: busy but broad panels let the ribbing read
Lower dark stripe on rockers frames it
Dark navy or black numbers read; white or pale numbers disappear into the ice, so avoid.
Plain stripes in dark navy or black: strong contrast on the pale base
Pairs well with: white, silver, navy, chrome.
pitfalls: Not fine speckle or snow static: it is chunky ribbed cells with dark seams
Not frosted glass: it is hard metallic, not soft translucent
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers in pale tones.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 219 (true metallic), roughness 80 (satin gloss), clearcoat 233 (almost no clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers in pale tones.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: plain stripes in dark navy or black: strong contrast on the pale base; big bold block graphics: calm areas against the busy cells
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter or flake: noise on noise; pale or white graphics: vanish into the ice
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat panel: smooth contrast zone; matte patches: calms the glint where numbers go
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
